title: Scheduled quota top-ups and tenant grace handling for reserved pools
creator: Ethan Cole
description: Implement scheduled quota top-up mechanism and tenant-level grace credit handling for Reserved Capacity pools. This ticket covers: 1) a deterministic scheduled job that issues proactive top-ups to tenant quota buckets at configurable cadences (daily/monthly/rolling-window offsets), 2) a bounded grace credit policy to absorb short-term spikes without immediate throttling, and 3) end-to-end accounting and audit trails so billing and reporting remain correct after top-ups and grace consumption.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can enqueue and execute top-up jobs for reserved pools with tenant scoping and idempotency
Top-up events produce an immutable audit record with before/after balances and correlation IDs
Grace credits are capped per tenant and decay deterministically (proportional decay) to avoid long-term credit accumulation
Rate limiter integrates with top-up state: a tenant may temporarily exceed per-minute target up to grace cap but is throttled once grace exhausted
Billing exports reconcile top-up and grace consumption so invoices match actual chargeable usage within 0.1% for sampled tenants
Can toggle feature via console flag per-organization for staged rollout and emergency disable
progress_updates: 2026-02-10: RFC drafted outlining scheduler semantics, grace model (fixed-credit vs proportional decay), and audit schema. Shared with Billing and Legal for feedback.

2026-02-17: Design review with Billing resulted in preference for proportional decay to avoid month-end credit hoarding. Decided to store top-up events as append-only rows in billing_events table with event_type 'top_up'
2026-02-22: Spike completed to validate idempotent scheduler using job fingerprinting. Implemented a test job and verified dedupe across restarts in staging
2026-03-01: Prototype rate-limiter hook implemented in serving runtime: checks live balance + grace allowance before admitting requests. Added metrics: grace_used, grace_exhausted_count

2026-03-05: QA found race where concurrent top-up and token consumption could undercount grace in-memory cache; mitigation plan is to make top-up updates commit to Redis then publish changelog event to update local caches
decisions: Use scheduled top-ups (cron-style) instead of real-time replenishment to reduce operational write amplification on billing DB
Grace policy will be a short-duration credit (configurable per-tenant) that decays proportionally each rolling window tick rather than a fixed refill at month boundary
Top-up and grace consumption must be represented in the single billing_events table to simplify downstream reconciliation and export pipelines
Expose emergency disable in Console and an API gate to prevent accidental global top-up during incidents
technical_notes: Schema: billing_events columns: id, tenant_id, event_type, amount, reason, created_at, correlation_id, source_job_id. Top-ups use reason='scheduled_topup' and include cadence metadata in source_job_id

Allocator flow: when scheduler triggers, compute tenant delta = target_reserved_quota - current_committed_quota, cap at tenant_max_topup, write billing_event row, then increment tenant_quota counter in Redis with optimized INCRBY semantics

Rate limiter integration: check pipeline will consult local Redis balance + grace_cache. If balance + grace_remaining >= request_cost then admit; otherwise reject. On top-up, publish a 'quota.change' message to service bus to update grace_cache atomically
Idempotency: top-up job fingerprint = sha256(pool_id + cadence + tenant_id + job_run_date). Upsert into jobs table keyed by fingerprint to prevent double issuance
Reconciliation: nightly job compares billing_events and Redis counters and emits anomalies report. Any drift > 0.5% opens auto-case to billing team
Telemetry: add metrics quota.topup.count, quota.topup.amount, quota.grace.used, quota.grace.exhausted, quota.reconcile.drift_rate
Backwards compatibility: default behaviour for tenants without opt-in remains current (no scheduled top-ups). Feature flag gating using ff-service key 'scheduled_quota_topups'
next_steps: Finish atomic Redis publish-subscribe change to eliminate race in cache updates (owner: Priya)
Instrument billing export tests that verify invoice parity on a 1,000-tenant sample (owner: Billing team)
Add console toggle and audit logging for enable/disable actions (owner: Console UX)
Schedule canary rollout: 5 pilot tenants on 2026-03-15, 50 tenants on 2026-03-22, full opt-in by 2026-04-05
